title: Effect of Novel Microalga‐Magnesium Amino Clay Nanoparticles on Municipal Wastewater Treatment and Pigments Production: An Integrated Approach
content:
ABSTRACT

This experimental study evaluates the behaviour of newly isolated microalgae Chlorella sorokiniana pa.91 grown in raw municipal wastewater with different concentrations of Magnesium Amino Clay Nano Particles (MgAC-NPs). The growth pattern of C. sorokiniana pa.91 to varying concentrations of MgAC-NPs at 0.0–1.0 g/L was investigated. Results showed that at a 0.2 g/L concentration, biomass concentration increased by 67.8% during 14-day cultivation. The effect of MgAC-NPs on the cell growth rate and the cell size was 0.2 1/day and 0.3–0.5 μm, respectively. Additionally, the results of MgAC-NPs adding show a removal efficiency of 96%, 90.6% and 91.1% for chemical oxygen demand (COD), ammonia (NH3) and phosphate (PO4 −3), respectively. The results showed that adding MgAC-NPs increased the removal efficiency for COD by 20%, but its effects on the removal efficiency of nutrients were insignificant.
